notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. The occasions of revelation (who the persons were, what happened) are not in the verses; they appear only under unknowns and uncertainties, as later tradition, with the hadith to add later. Pronouns the Arabic leaves open are left open. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: There are those who took a mosque for harm, for disbelief, for dividing the believers, and as a place of lying in wait for one who had fought God and His messenger before.
They will swear that they wanted only the best, and God bears witness that they are liars.
The one addressed is told never to stand in it.
A mosque founded on piety from the first day is more worthy of his standing in it; in it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves.

The verse asks whether one who founded his building on fear of God and His approval is better, or one who founded it on the edge of a crumbling bank, which collapsed with him into the fire of Hell; God does not guide the wrongdoing people.
The building they built will not cease to be a doubt in their hearts, until their hearts are cut into pieces; God is knowing and wise.

chapters.summary_md: The verses speak of those who took a mosque for harm, for disbelief and for dividing the believers [c1]. They say that God bears witness that these people are liars when they swear that they wanted only the best [c2]. The one addressed is told never to stand in it [c3], and the verses speak of a mosque founded on piety from the first day [c4].
chapters.body_md:
There are those who took a mosque for harm, for disbelief, for dividing the believers, and as a place of lying in wait for one who had fought God and His messenger before [c1]. They will swear that they wanted only the best, and God bears witness that they are liars [c2].

The one addressed is told never to stand in it [c3]. A mosque founded on piety from the first day is more worthy of his standing in it; in it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves [c4].

The verse asks whether one who founded his building on fear of God and His approval is better, or one who founded it on the edge of a crumbling bank, which collapsed with him into the fire of Hell; God does not guide the wrongdoing people [c5]. The building they built will not cease to be a doubt in their hearts, until their hearts are cut into pieces; God is knowing and wise [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The passage names the purposes of those who built it: harm, disbelief, division and lying in wait [c1]. It reports what they will swear and God's witness against it [c2]. It then sets buildings side by side, one founded on piety and one on the edge of a crumbling bank [c4][c5]. It does not name the builders, the place, or the one they lay in wait for [c1].
chapters.kids_md: The verses speak of people who took a mosque for harm and to divide the believers [c1]. They say that a mosque founded on piety is more worthy [c4]. They say that in it are men who love to purify themselves, and that God loves those who purify themselves [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage judges a building by what it was founded on: piety and God's approval on one side, harm and division on the other [c1][c5]. Another is that it speaks of purifying oneself as something God loves [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: where the mosque stood, who built it, when, or what became of it. The verses give none of this.
- Not established: who 'one who had fought God and His messenger before' is.
- Not established: which mosque is 'founded on piety from the first day', or who the men are who love to purify themselves.
- Not established: whether 'stand in it' refers to prayer; the verse says only 'stand'.
- Not established: what the 'doubt in their hearts' refers to beyond the words of 9:110.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the builders, the place, the occasion and what followed. None is used in the story texts.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated reports on the occasion of these ayat, on the builders and the place and on what was done with the building, each with a named grader. None is used in this draft.
The statement about those who built it (9:107) and the image of 9:109 are stated in the verses' own words; a scholar should decide whether the kids text should keep them.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identity of the builders, of the one they lay in wait for and of the mosque founded on piety.
